question: Imagine you almost give an oral syrup through an intravenous (IV) line by mistake. Which medication right did you almost break?

options.A: Right Documentation
options.B: Right Route
options.C: Right Dose
options.D: Right Time

explanation: The 'Right Route' means giving the drug through the exact pathway the doctor ordered (like oral versus IV). Always double-check how the drug is supposed to enter the body!

question: Why is community participation essential for the long-term success of public health interventions?

options.A: Traditional beliefs make outside nurses unwelcome without local approval
options.B: Local residents ensure facilities like water pumps are maintained after external aid projects end
options.C: Government health budgets are too small to pay local workers for maintenance
options.D: International donors refuse to send money unless villagers sign a legal contract

explanation: When communities take ownership, they maintain and protect health infrastructure long after initial external projects conclude. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T14#GNS313_U1_T14_h7)

question: Which of these is a classic sign of postpartum endometritis (infection of the uterus lining)?

options.A: Sudden weight gain and facial swelling
options.B: Foul-smelling lochia and fever
options.C: High blood pressure and visual changes
options.D: Painful urination and flank pain

explanation: When the uterine lining gets infected, it usually lets you know through fever, tenderness, and vaginal discharge that smells unusual or foul. You're building great clinical instincts! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h5)

question: What determines whether a person is considered Rh-positive?

options.A: The presence of the D antigen on their red blood cells
options.B: The presence of anti-Rh antibodies floating in their plasma
options.C: The presence of both A and B antigens on their platelets
options.D: The total volume of hemoglobin circulating in their blood

explanation: The term Rh-positive simply means the red blood cells carry the D antigen on their outer surface. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T8#GNS123_U2_T8_h3)

question: Why do healthcare workers count out loud before doing a lift together?

options.A: It helps everyone lift together at the exact same moment
options.B: It distracts the patient from feeling any pain
options.C: It signals visitors to leave the room quietly
options.D: It measures the exact seconds the transfer takes

explanation: Teamwork makes the dream work! Counting down ensures everyone pulls or lifts in unison so nobody drops the weight.

question: Why is diet therapy such an important part of your daily nursing duties?

options.A: Nurses must personally cook all meals served in the hospital ward
options.B: Nurses are responsible for monitoring patient tolerance and supporting the prescribed nutrition plan
options.C: Dietary plans replace the need for physical assessments
options.D: Doctors never check what patients are eating

explanation: Since you spend the most time with patients, you are in the best position to see if they are enjoying their food and how well their body is handling it!

question: Why does severe liver disease (cirrhosis) often lead to higher levels of active oral drugs in the bloodstream?

options.A: Reduced liver metabolism bypasses normal first-pass breakdown
options.B: The damaged liver absorbs extra medication directly from meals
options.C: Heart output speeds up to push drugs past the liver faster
options.D: Cirrhosis increases the production of helpful blood proteins

explanation: Normally, the liver acts as a checkpoint for oral drugs (first-pass metabolism). If the liver is scarred or failing, it fails to break down its usual share, sending a flood of active drug straight into circulation. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T10#GNS125_U5_T10_h5)

question: Which body tissue is mainly responsible for movement and pumping blood?

options.A: Nervous tissue
options.B: Muscle tissue
options.C: Connective tissue
options.D: Epithelial tissue

explanation: Muscle tissue is built to contract and shorten, making it the powerhouse behind every movement you make.

question: A clinic spends its limited budget on new vaccines instead of fixing a leaking roof. What is the opportunity cost here?

options.A: The total financial value of the newly purchased vaccines
options.B: The electricity used to power the vaccine storage refrigerator
options.C: The salary paid to the clinic manager for making the choice
options.D: The protection and comfort lost from delaying the roof repair

explanation: Since they chose vaccines, the opportunity cost is the benefit they missed out on by leaving the roof unfixed for now.

question: What is the term for the grating sound heard when broken bone ends rub together?

options.A: Cyanosis
options.B: Contracture
options.C: Crepitus
options.D: Clonus

explanation: Crepitus is the distinctive crunchy sound or sensation produced when rough ends of fractured bone rub together. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T13#GNS221_U3_T13_h3)

question: Why do special children typically require care that goes beyond routine pediatric visits?

options.A: Standard pediatric clinics do not admit children with chronic illnesses
options.B: They have complex developmental, physical, or chronic health conditions
options.C: Special children only need care during emergency situations
options.D: Routine checkups are completely unnecessary after the first year of life

explanation: Their unique health profiles demand coordinated, specialized interventions rather than standard checkups alone. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h1)

question: Which psychological condition is often seen in women and girls who have survived FGM?

options.A: Bipolar manic depression with hallucinations
options.B: Obsessive compulsive cleaning disorder
options.C: Post-traumatic stress disorder and anxiety
options.D: Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder

explanation: Spot on! The painful and terrifying experience often leaves survivors with long-term emotional trauma, anxiety, and distress.

question: Why does recovery from an axonotmesis injury take many months to occur?

options.A: Inflammation must completely clear out of the central nervous system before peripheral signals are allowed to pass.
options.B: Specialized white blood cells must first convert the damaged myelin into functional scar tissue.
options.C: The body has to completely rebuild the surrounding bone structure before nerve fibers can begin to cross the gap.
options.D: The regrowing axon must slowly creep down the remaining connective tube at a rate of about one millimeter per day.

explanation: Axonal regeneration is a very slow biological process, requiring months for fibers to travel from the injury site all the way back to muscles in the feet or hands. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T18#GNS222_U3_T18_h3)

question: As a nursing student, how should you easily tell the difference between 'morbidity' and 'mortality'?

options.A: Morbidity is a statistic while mortality is a clinical diagnosis
options.B: Morbidity refers to illness while mortality refers to death
options.C: Morbidity affects only infants while mortality affects mothers
options.D: Morbidity is always preventable while mortality is inevitable

explanation: Think of it this way: morbidity means being sick or having health complications, while mortality simply means death. Simple and clear!

question: A nurse discards an empty glass drug ampoule. Which waste category does this item belong to?

options.A: Food waste
options.B: Sharps
options.C: Paper waste
options.D: General waste

explanation: Even though ampoules are glass rather than needles, their sharp edges can easily cut skin, so they must be treated as sharps waste. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T15#GNS122_U3_T15_h2)

question: Why do nurses perform a full assessment when a new resident is admitted to a care facility?

options.A: To establish a baseline and identify individual health risks
options.B: To diagnose new acute infectious diseases
options.C: To determine the exact date the resident will be discharged
options.D: To fulfill a legal requirement without affecting care

explanation: Great job! This initial check helps you know what is 'normal' for the resident so you can easily spot things like fall risks early on.

question: How long do patients usually need antibiotic treatment for infective endocarditis?

options.A: Four to six weeks
options.B: Six months to a year
options.C: One to two weeks
options.D: Three to five days

explanation: Germs hiding inside heart valve growths are very hard for drugs to reach. That's why patients need a long course of IV antibiotics, usually 4 to 6 weeks.

question: A nurse finishes drawing up an emergency medication from a single-dose vial. What should be done with the remaining liquid in the vial?

options.A: Save it in the pocket for the next patient
options.B: Put it back into the main supply drawer
options.C: Discard the leftover portion immediately
options.D: Leave the syringe attached for later use

explanation: Single-dose vials do not contain preservatives, so any leftover medication must be thrown away to prevent microbial growth. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T6#GNS122_U3_T6_h2)

question: What is the absolute first thing a nurse must do when a patient arrives with complications from an unsafe abortion?

options.A: Stabilizing airway, breathing, and circulation
options.B: Filling out legal police reports immediately
options.C: Conducting a detailed religious counseling session
options.D: Interrogating the patient about who performed the procedure

explanation: ABC comes first in every emergency! Saving the patient's life and treating shock always takes priority over asking questions.

question: How does poor eating over time affect the health of a community?

options.A: It increases physical strength through muscle adaptation
options.B: It stabilizes local healthcare infrastructure automatically
options.C: It weakens body defenses and speeds up chronic illnesses
options.D: It completely eliminates the risk of communicable diseases

explanation: Spot on! Lacking essential nutrients leaves people more open to long-term conditions like high blood pressure and diabetes, putting a heavy load on local health systems.

question: A hypertensive patient keeps missing clinic days and stopped taking their drugs. As their nurse, what is your best next step?

options.A: Assume the patient is completely cured and stop calling their phone number
options.B: Conduct a home visit to discuss barriers to compliance and provide tailored education
options.C: Discharge the patient permanently from the clinic registry without further discussion
options.D: Report the patient to local law enforcement authorities for policy violation

explanation: Wonderful nursing judgment! Visiting them helps you find out why they stopped—maybe money is tight or side effects are bothering them—so you can help find a solution together.

question: A nurse teaches primary school pupils about handwashing. Six weeks later, she checks if the rate of diarrhea among the children has dropped. What type of evaluation is this?

options.A: Financial budgeting
options.B: Impact evaluation
options.C: Logistical planning
options.D: Baseline assessment

explanation: Spot on! Looking at long-term health changes—like a drop in illness rates—tells you the real impact your teaching made.

question: Which chemical messenger in the brain primarily acts to inhibit electrical activity and calm neurons down?

options.A: Sodium
options.B: Glutamate
options.C: GABA
options.D: Calcium

explanation: GABA is the main inhibitory neurotransmitter that helps prevent excessive electrical firing in the brain. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T16#GNS222_U3_T16_h2)

question: What is the primary rule when examining a limb for musculoskeletal problems?

options.A: Always use a goniometer during the initial inspection phase
options.B: Always examine the lower extremities before the upper extremities
options.C: Always start by performing an X-ray before touching the limb
options.D: Always compare the affected side with the unaffected side

explanation: Comparing the injured or painful limb to the healthy side gives the nurse a baseline of what is normal for that specific patient. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T3#GNS222_U1_T3_h1)

question: Which nursing intervention is most helpful for an outpatient struggling to remember multiple pills at different times?

options.A: Organizing the medications into a weekly pill organizer box
options.B: Instructing the patient to stop taking all drugs until the next clinic visit
options.C: Doubling the dose the next morning to make up for missed pills
options.D: Switching all oral medications to intravenous administration at home

explanation: Pill organizers provide a visual cue and physical structure that makes daily dosing straightforward and easy to monitor. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T2#GNS215_U4_T2_h6)

question: What is the nurse's main job right after a tissue sample (biopsy) is taken?

options.A: Place the tissue sample in a household refrigerator until the morning shift
options.B: Examine the cells under the ward microscope to give an early report
options.C: Wash the specimen with sterile water to remove any residual blood
options.D: Ensure correct labeling and prompt placement in the proper preservative solution

explanation: Good lab results start with proper handling! Labeling it right away and putting it in the right preservative keeps the sample safe for testing.

question: What actually happens during an intrauterine insemination (IUI) procedure?

options.A: A hormonal patch is applied to the abdomen to trigger ovulation
options.B: Mature eggs are harvested directly from the ovaries using a needle
options.C: Fertilized embryos are surgically placed directly into the fallopian tubes
options.D: Washed sperm is placed straight into the uterine cavity using a thin catheter

explanation: You nailed it! IUI helps by placing prepared sperm right inside the uterus, giving them a shorter trip to the egg. Keep it up!

question: Which two mental health conditions are most commonly diagnosed in people living with HIV?

options.A: Schizophrenia and bipolar disorder
options.B: Obsessive-compulsive disorder and phobias
options.C: Anorexia nervosa and bulimia
options.D: Depression and anxiety

explanation: Dealing with a chronic illness and facing social judgment can understandably take a toll, often leading to depression and anxiety.

question: A patient with a leg cast complains of severe itching deep inside the cast. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: Tell the patient to pour warm water down the cast to wash away the itchy skin cells
options.B: Cut the cast off immediately because itching means a severe infection is present
options.C: Instruct the patient never to insert objects inside and suggest using a cool hair dryer setting
options.D: Provide a long knitting needle wrapped in cotton gauze so they can scratch safely

explanation: Foreign objects can break fragile skin inside the cast and introduce bacteria, while cool air safely relieves itching without harming the skin. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T13#GNS221_U3_T13_h7)

question: When is it legally and ethically okay to break patient confidentiality?

options.A: When a curious coworker asks about a patient's diagnosis
options.B: When family members demand updates over the telephone
options.C: When the nurse wants to gossip about a famous admission
options.D: When the patient poses an immediate danger to self or others

explanation: Well done! Safety always comes first—if someone is in immediate danger of harm, confidentiality rules can be bypassed to keep people safe.

question: When checking blood tests for primary hypothyroidism, which result do you expect to see?

options.A: Decreased serum thyrotropin-releasing hormone
options.B: Decreased serum thyroid-stimulating hormone
options.C: Elevated serum thyroxine levels
options.D: Elevated serum thyroid-stimulating hormone

explanation: Think of the pituitary gland as a boss trying to get a lazy thyroid to work. When the thyroid slows down, the boss shouts louder by pumping out extra TSH! So a high TSH level is the main clue for primary hypothyroidism.

question: During a clinic health talk, you want to recommend affordable local Nigerian foods rich in iron. Which of these is best?

options.A: Carbonated soft drinks and sweetened juices
options.B: Processed white bread and sugary snacks
options.C: Dark green leafy vegetables and lean meats
options.D: Polished white rice and refined cassava flour

explanation: Fantastic! Local greens like ugu, ewedu, and green amaranth, paired with lean meats, are packed with natural iron to keep pregnant mums strong and healthy.

question: Why do pregnant women routinely need iron supplements during gestation?

options.A: To harden the bones of the mother's hands and feet
options.B: To increase the amount of amniotic fluid in the womb
options.C: To support the significant increase in maternal blood volume
options.D: To prevent the baby from developing gestational diabetes

explanation: Spot on! A pregnant woman's body makes a lot more blood to support the baby, and iron helps prevent anemia during this heavy workload.

question: Which finding is a normal vascular change expected during a routine prenatal checkup?

options.A: Sudden widespread purpura and bruising
options.B: Small spider angiomas on the upper chest
options.C: Painful deep purple nodules on the calves
options.D: Complete absence of blood flow to the fingers

explanation: Spotting small spider-like blood vessels (angiomas) is super common due to extra blood volume and high estrogen during pregnancy. Nothing to worry about!

question: What is the golden rule regarding organisational strategy and structure?

options.A: Strategy must follow structure
options.B: Strategy changes before employees arrive
options.C: Structure and strategy are unrelated
options.D: Structure must follow strategy

explanation: An organisation always builds its structure to support its main goals (strategy), not the other way around!

question: What is a major perk of getting your vitamins from real food instead of pills?

options.A: Pills are always completely fake and contain no actual vitamins
options.B: Whole foods provide fiber and a complex nutritional matrix
options.C: Whole foods cost nothing at all to produce or purchase
options.D: Pills take up to a week to dissolve in the human stomach

explanation: Spot on! Whole foods come with extra bonuses like fiber and natural plant compounds that supplements just can't copy.

question: Why does keeping a young married girl away from her friends and family hurt her mental health so much?

options.A: It forces her to make independent financial decisions
options.B: It cuts off her normal support system of friends and family
options.C: It provides her with too much free time to worry
options.D: It eliminates all contact with healthcare workers

explanation: Taking a child away from school and peers destroys her support network, leaving her all alone to handle adult stress.

question: Which tool is used to hold the surgical needle securely when repairing an episiotomy?

options.A: Needle holder
options.B: Mucus extractor
options.C: Anatomical fetoscope
options.D: Cord scissors

explanation: A needle holder gives you a firm, non-slip grip so you can pass your stitches smoothly and comfortably.

question: During which part of pregnancy do a mother's daily food energy (calorie) needs go up the most?

options.A: Third trimester
options.B: The first two weeks postpartum
options.C: During active labor
options.D: First trimester

explanation: As the baby gets bigger towards the end of pregnancy, calorie needs peak—demanding extra energy to cross the finish line!

question: Why does someone struggling with long-term drug use need larger doses over time to get the same high?

options.A: The kidneys begin filtering the chemical out of the blood much faster
options.B: The brain reduces its own dopamine production and receptor sites to adapt
options.C: The liver starts storing the drug in fat tissues instead of breaking it down
options.D: The stomach lining thickens and blocks the drug from entering the bloodstream

explanation: Brilliant! This is tolerance in action. The brain tries to protect itself from massive chemical floods by muting its own receptors, meaning you need more of the drug just to feel normal.

question: What was a major benefit when hospital-based home care programs first started?

options.A: They allowed patients to leave expensive hospital beds earlier while still receiving care
options.B: They completely eliminated the need for outpatient physician clinics
options.C: They removed all financial costs for the patients receiving treatment
options.D: They allowed nurses to perform major surgeries inside private residences

explanation: Extending hospital care into people's homes helped free up expensive hospital beds for sicker patients while keeping costs down.

question: What is the best way for a nurse to start talking with a patient who has just suffered a heavy loss?

options.A: Provide a printed checklist of grief stages for the patient to fill out
options.B: Wait in silence until the patient explicitly asks for medical advice
options.C: Tell the patient about your own personal losses to build quick rapport
options.D: Ask open-ended questions and listen actively to the patient's story

explanation: You got it! Open-ended questions open the door for patients to share their unique story without feeling pressured or rushed.

question: What happens to body cells when a hypotonic IV solution is infused into the vascular system?

options.A: Fluid is pulled out of the cells into the bloodstream, causing them to shrink.
options.B: Water molecules stay completely inside the blood vessels with no movement.
options.C: Fluid moves from the blood vessels into the cells, causing them to swell.
options.D: Red blood cells immediately break apart and release all their hemoglobin.

explanation: Hypotonic solutions have a lower concentration of solutes than blood, so water shifts toward areas of higher solute concentration inside the cells. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T16#GNS122_U1_T16_h3)

question: Which action must a nurse take BEFORE giving a high-risk medication?

options.A: Ask the patient to sign a waiver releasing the hospital from liability
options.B: Gather baseline clinical data and relevant lab values
options.C: Discontinue all other medications the patient is currently taking
options.D: Double the prescribed dose to test for allergic reactions

explanation: Baseline checks give you a reference point to compare against if the patient develops adverse symptoms later. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T2#GNS215_U5_T2_h6)

question: What does nutrient utilisation mean in the human body?

options.A: Storing excess fat directly beneath the skin layers
options.B: The rapid excretion of waste products through the kidneys
options.C: The physical chewing and swallowing of solid meals
options.D: Converting ingested food into energy and structural components

explanation: You've got this! Nutrient utilisation is simply how the body takes down food molecules and turns them into useful energy and building blocks for the body.

question: Why do nurses use slide sheets when moving a patient from a bed to a stretcher?

options.A: They replace the need for any nurses to assist
options.B: They act as a heating pad to warm up the patient
options.C: They automatically record the patient's weight
options.D: They reduce friction and shearing forces on the patient's skin

explanation: Slide sheets are a nurse's best friend! They make patients glide smoothly, protecting fragile skin from friction and saving your back from strain.

question: What is an important food safety habit a nurse should teach families to prevent cross-contamination?

options.A: Reusing cooking oil indefinitely without filtering it
options.B: Keeping raw foods and cooked foods strictly separated
options.C: Washing all kitchen knives with cold water only
options.D: Storing all fresh vegetables inside closed plastic bags in the sun

explanation: Always keep raw meats away from ready-to-eat meals so harmful bacteria don't hitch a ride onto your food.

question: What physical pushing force drives fluid and tiny particles out of blood capillaries and into tissues?

options.A: Active transport
options.B: Hydrostatic pressure
options.C: Osmotic pull
options.D: Oncotic pressure

explanation: You nailed it! Hydrostatic pressure is simply the physical pushing pressure of blood flowing through your vessels, forcing fluid out into the tissues.

question: What is a major transport-related challenge that often contributes to maternal deaths in Nigeria?

options.A: Excessive availability of fully equipped ambulances in villages
options.B: Too many doctors available at primary healthcare centers
options.C: Delays in transportation and reaching a medical facility
options.D: Immediate acceptance of patients at tertiary hospitals

explanation: Getting stuck trying to find transport to a hospital (the famous 'second delay') is a huge hurdle in saving mothers in remote areas.

question: You need to give a routine vaccine to a 12-month-old baby. Which site should you use?

options.A: Deltoid
options.B: Dorsogluteal
options.C: Vastus lateralis
options.D: Ventrogluteal

explanation: Brilliant! The vastus lateralis (outer thigh) is well-developed in infants and is the recommended spot for their routine immunizations.

question: What happens when health programs are copied from other regions without a local diagnosis?

options.A: They become cheaper for the local government to maintain
options.B: They automatically succeed because health problems are identical everywhere
options.C: They eliminate all infectious diseases within a single month
options.D: They may fail because they do not fit the local culture or environment

explanation: Every community is unique; interventions that work in one setting can easily fail if applied blindly elsewhere without local data. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T3#GNS124_U3_T3_h5)

question: What is the main danger nurses must watch out for in elderly patients undergoing heavy bowel cleansing?

options.A: Dehydration and electrolyte imbalance from losing too much fluid
options.B: High blood pressure caused by laxatives
options.C: Sudden weight gain from water holding in the skin
options.D: Permanent paralysis of the large intestine muscles

explanation: Strong laxatives and clear liquids cause quick bowel emptying, which can easily dry out and weaken older adults.

question: Why does a midwife perform a gentle rectal exam after a delivery?

options.A: To evaluate the baseline tone of the pelvic floor muscles
options.B: To stimulate uterine contractions and prevent postpartum bleeding
options.C: To check if the anal sphincter and rectal mucosa are injured
options.D: To ensure the placenta has been completely expelled

explanation: It's a quick and necessary check to make sure a deep tear hasn't hidden itself by extending into the anal sphincter or rectal wall.

question: Which test is commonly used to check a patient's long-term blood sugar control over the past three months?

options.A: Hemoglobin A1c assay
options.B: Serum potassium level
options.C: Urinalysis for protein
options.D: Complete blood count

explanation: Correct! The HbA1c test gives us a wonderful 3-month picture of how well blood glucose has been managed.

question: How does a nurse best show public health advocacy regarding breathing disorders?

options.A: Doing deep lung biopsies in local health clinics
options.B: Isolating every single person with a seasonal flu
options.C: Supporting policies that cut down air pollution and tobacco use
options.D: Prescribing strong bronchodilators to people in the neighborhood

explanation: Advocacy goes beyond the hospital bedside. Nurses advocate by supporting healthier environments, clean air policies, and community tobacco control.

question: What vital equipment must always be kept ready at the bedside of a patient recovering from an airway issue?

options.A: A standard blood pressure cuff and stethoscope
options.B: Suction machine and a manual breathing bag
options.C: A sterile surgical tray for major tummy surgery
options.D: An intravenous infusion pump with extra tubing

explanation: Always be prepared! Having suction and a bag-valve-mask right at the bedside lets nurses act instantly if thick mucus blocks the airway or breathing slows down.

question: Which of these is a dangerous medication habit that you should warn patients against?

options.A: Checking expiration dates on packaging before swallowing pills
options.B: Reporting any unusual itching or rashes to your healthcare provider
options.C: Sharing your leftover antibiotics with sick family members
options.D: Completing the entire dose prescribed by a qualified doctor

explanation: Never share your drugs! Dosage needs vary from person to person, and what cures your infection could harm someone else.

question: What is the main focus of a maternity home in the community?

options.A: Managing low-risk pregnancies and normal deliveries
options.B: Treating chronic illnesses in elderly patients
options.C: Performing major complex obstetric surgeries
options.D: Providing long-term pediatric intensive care

explanation: You've got this! Maternity homes are set up to handle normal, healthy pregnancies and deliveries right in the neighborhood.

question: A teenage client is super shy and hesitant to talk about sexual health. What should you do first as their nurse?

options.A: Create a safe, confidential, and non-judgmental environment
options.B: Call the client's parents into the room immediately
options.C: Skip the sexual health assessment entirely
options.D: Scold the client for being immature about health matters

explanation: Brilliant nursing instinct! Trust and a warm, welcoming vibe help nervous clients relax and open up to care.

question: Which sociological theory suggests that older adults remain happier and healthier when they stay busy and socially involved?

options.A: Free radical theory
options.B: Activity theory
options.C: Disengagement theory
options.D: Wear-and-tear theory

explanation: Activity theory proposes that staying socially active and maintaining roles promotes well-being in older age. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T1#GNS321_U3_T1_h3)

question: Why is prevention so important in cancer care?

options.A: It replaces the need for surgical removal of tumors in every single patient.
options.B: It completely eliminates the requirement for diagnostic lab testing.
options.C: It stops the disease early, reducing suffering and healthcare costs.
options.D: It guarantees that patients will never experience any genetic mutations in their lifetime.

explanation: Preventing cancer or catching it early spares your future patients from aggressive treatments and helps them live longer, healthier lives.

question: How do long-acting injectable antipsychotics make community care easier?

options.A: They can be administered without any medical professional present
options.B: They completely eliminate all possible side effects of the medication
options.C: They remove the need for daily pill-taking and ensure steady medication levels
options.D: They cure the underlying genetic cause of the psychotic disorder

explanation: You're doing great! Injectables save patients from swallowing pills every single day and keep their drug levels nice and steady.

question: When anticholinergic drugs block the parasympathetic nervous system, which body response naturally takes over?

options.A: Normal resting state
options.B: Fight-or-flight response
options.C: Basal metabolic state
options.D: Rest and digest response

explanation: You've got it! Blocking the 'rest and digest' system lets the sympathetic 'fight-or-flight' responses take the lead.

question: How are blood-borne infections like HIV and Hepatitis B mainly spread during traditional FGM?

options.A: Exposure to contaminated air in rural communities
options.B: Drinking contaminated water after the procedure
options.C: Insect bites during outdoor healing rituals
options.D: Reusing unsterilized cutting instruments on multiple individuals

explanation: Spot on! Using the same knife or razor blade for different girls without cleaning it passes blood and infections directly between them.

question: How do Integrase Strand Transfer Inhibitors (INSTIs) stop HIV from multiplying?

options.A: By destroying red blood cells in the bloodstream
options.B: By preventing viral DNA from inserting into the host cell's DNA
options.C: By changing the patient's blood type permanently
options.D: By blocking the patient from feeling hungry

explanation: You got it! INSTIs block the 'integrase' enzyme, which the virus uses like glue to paste its own genetic code into our human cells.

question: Which major body cavity contains both the heart and the lungs?

options.A: Thoracic cavity
options.B: Vertebral cavity
options.C: Abdominopelvic cavity
options.D: Cranial cavity

explanation: The thoracic cavity is located in the upper chest and houses the lungs, heart, and major blood vessels. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h5)

question: An adolescent health clinic welcomes all teenagers regardless of their financial status or background. Which core characteristic is this clinic showing?

options.A: Selective
options.B: Commercial
options.C: Exclusive
options.D: Equitable

explanation: Equitable care simply means fair treatment for every young person, treating everyone with equal care and without any form of discrimination.

question: Why do patients experience shortness of breath when they have a respiratory problem?

options.A: The kidneys are retaining too much water
options.B: The heart is pumping too much blood to the muscles
options.C: The stomach is pushing upward against the diaphragm
options.D: The body is trying to fix low oxygen or high carbon dioxide levels

explanation: Think of shortness of breath as an alarm bell! It's your body's clever way of telling you it needs more oxygen or needs to blow off extra carbon dioxide. Great effort!

question: What is the golden rule of nursing documentation when it comes to legal protection?

options.A: If it was not charted, it was not done
options.B: Only write down abnormal patient vitals
options.C: Always erase mistakes with correction fluid
options.D: Chart at the end of the week from memory

explanation: In the eyes of the law, if you didn't write it down in the chart, it never happened. Document everything you do!

question: Why is a functional referral system necessary for family planning clients?

options.A: It ensures safe, continuous care when a client needs specialized services

options.C: It guarantees that clients never have to pay for their contraceptive drugs
options.D: It eliminates the need for nurses to provide health education at primary clinics

explanation: Referrals link primary care clinics to advanced facilities, ensuring clients get appropriate treatment without dropping out of care. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T029#GNS226_U6_T029_h1)

question: Why is infection control particularly challenging during home care procedures?

options.A: Household factors like pets and limited space increase contamination risks
options.B: Patients are immune to standard hospital-grade sanitizing agents
options.C: Sterile equipment cannot legally be brought into private residences
options.D: Water supplies in homes lack any form of bacterial filtration

explanation: Unlike sterile hospital rooms, homes contain everyday clutter, family members, and pets that make maintaining a clean field harder. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T7#GNS324_U1_T7_h4)

question: Why is disease surveillance often called an early warning system?

options.A: It predicts exact weather conditions for disease outbreaks.
options.B: It helps health workers spot unusual patterns before an epidemic grows.
options.C: It automatically cures patients before they visit the hospital.
options.D: It replaces the need for laboratory testing entirely.

explanation: Spotting rising cases early lets health workers jump in and take action before a tiny bump turns into a full-blown outbreak!

question: Which mineral shortage causes anemia and makes it hard for children to focus and learn?

options.A: Potassium
options.B: Zinc
options.C: Calcium
options.D: Iron

explanation: You got it! Iron helps make hemoglobin to carry oxygen around the body. Without enough of it, kids feel tired and find it tough to concentrate.

question: An infant is brought to the clinic for routine immunization at 9 months old. Which key vaccine is due at this visit?

options.A: Measles vaccine
options.B: Pentavalent booster dose four
options.C: First dose of BCG
options.D: Oral polio vaccine dose zero

explanation: Spot on! The first dose of the measles vaccine is scheduled right at 9 months to keep growing babies safe.

question: Why do doctors frequently order a chest CT scan for a patient diagnosed with osteosarcoma?

options.A: To screen for concurrent rib fractures
options.B: To measure the exact length of the femur
options.C: To check for early metastasis to the lungs
options.D: To evaluate heart function before surgery

explanation: Osteosarcoma cells love to travel through the bloodstream, and the lungs are one of their favorite places to land. Checking the chest early is super important!

question: What is the big advantage of giving tumor chemotherapy through an artery instead of a vein?

options.A: It completely eliminates all side effects throughout the entire body
options.B: It delivers a higher concentration of the drug directly to the tumor site
options.C: It prevents the drug from ever entering the systemic circulation
options.D: It allows the patient to take the chemotherapy medication at home

explanation: Think of it like dropping the medicine right on the doorstep of the problem! It gives the tumor a concentrated dose before the blood carries it away.

question: What is the best way to cook green vegetables while keeping their water-soluble vitamins intact?

options.A: By soaking them in cold water for several hours before cooking
options.B: By frying them at high temperatures in vegetable oil
options.C: By boiling them rapidly in a large pot of uncovered water
options.D: By steaming them gently using a minimal amount of water

explanation: Steaming keeps veggies away from a direct bath of boiling water, helping them hold on to their wholesome nutrients.

question: Which nutrient is most critical for building and repairing muscle tissue in our patients?

options.A: Sodium chloride
options.B: Vitamin C
options.C: Protein
options.D: Complex fiber

explanation: Protein is the body's building block! It provides the essential amino acids required to repair existing muscle fibers and build new ones.

question: A patient is using a vaginal antifungal cream. What crucial contraceptive safety advice must you share with her?

options.A: Barrier methods must be completely avoided for three months
options.B: Condoms will dissolve instantly upon contact with vaginal tissue
options.C: The medication completely inactivates oral contraceptive pills
options.D: The cream can weaken latex condoms and diaphragms

explanation: The oils in many vaginal creams can damage latex. Always warn patients that condoms might break so they can stay protected!

question: What lab tests must a nurse check before giving cytotoxic drugs?

options.A: Stool cultures and routine lipid panels
options.B: Urinary calcium and serum protein counts
options.C: Blood glucose and thyroid hormone levels
options.D: Complete blood count and organ function tests

explanation: Wonderful! We always check blood counts and kidney/liver labs first to make sure the patient's body can safely handle the medicine.

question: Why must nurse managers be careful with how much time is spent in meetings?

options.A: Because clinical staff prefer attending meetings over working on the ward
options.B: Because hospital accreditation bodies require a specific number of meeting hours
options.C: Because meetings are the only way to evaluate nurse performance
options.D: Because poorly run meetings pull staff away from patient care without adding value

explanation: Every minute in a meeting is time away from the bedside. Good managers make sure meetings are truly worth it!

question: Which of these is NOT a typical complication of an untreated liver hydatid cyst?

options.A: Rupture into the peritoneal cavity
options.B: Biliary tract obstruction
options.C: Permanent vision loss
options.D: Secondary bacterial infection

explanation: Liver cysts cause tummy, bile duct, and belly issues—they don't mess with your eyesight!

question: Why might a severely anemic patient NOT show a blue skin color (cyanosis) even when their oxygen is dangerously low?

options.A: Their skin is naturally thicker and hides color changes better
options.B: Anemia causes the blood vessels to dilate and turn the skin red instead
options.C: They do not have enough red blood cells or hemoglobin to display the blue color
options.D: Their lungs absorb extra oxygen from the surrounding air

explanation: You're getting the hang of it! Cyanosis needs enough hemoglobin (the stuff in red blood cells that carries oxygen) to show that blue tint. If a patient is severely anemic, they simply don't have enough to show the color!

question: Why do we use standard precautions in the hospital ward?

options.A: To lower the cost of purchasing expensive surgical gloves
options.B: To reduce the risk of transmitting infections from body fluids
options.C: To treat patients who have diagnosed infectious diseases
options.D: To completely eliminate bacteria from the hospital ward

explanation: You've got this! Standard precautions are our everyday shield to stop germs in blood and body fluids from spreading to us or other patients.

question: You notice on your monthly report that many young clients are skipping their second injectable dose. What is the best action to take?

options.A: Stop ordering injectable contraceptives for the clinic entirely
options.B: Organize community education and strengthen client reminder systems
options.C: Refuse care to any client who misses an appointment date
options.D: Wait until the federal ministry sends a special investigation team

explanation: Wonderful clinical thinking! Spotting a trend like missed doses means we should step up our appointment reminders and patient counseling.

question: Why do community health nurses keep a close eye on people living in the same house as a leprosy patient?

options.A: They are forced to pay for the patient's hospital bills
options.B: They are at higher risk because they spend so much time together
options.C: They are legally banned from leaving the house during treatment
options.D: They must swallow preventive antibiotics for years

explanation: Living closely under one roof means more exposure time, so checking family members regularly helps catch any early signs. Fantastic job completing this set!

question: What is the main job of the pudendal nerve during ejaculation?

options.A: Producing primary male sex hormones
options.B: Filtering toxins from seminal fluid
options.C: Controlling somatic pelvic floor muscles for expulsion
options.D: Stopping blood flow to the testes

explanation: Spot on! The pudendal nerve talks to the pelvic floor muscles, telling them to do those rhythmic squeezes that push semen out.

question: Why do nurses need to handle strong chemical sterilants like glutaraldehyde with extra care?

options.A: They instantly blow up under bright theatre lamps
options.B: They can cause bad skin rashes, irritation, and breathing trouble
options.C: They completely cancel out the local anaesthetic given to patients
options.D: They melt stainless steel instruments into liquid on contact

explanation: Potent disinfectants are harsh on living cells! We always need good ventilation and protective gear to keep these chemicals away from our skin and lungs.

question: What is the main purpose of a pre-placement medical examination?

options.A: To determine the final retirement pension of the employee
options.B: To establish a baseline health status before job exposure begins
options.C: To diagnose casual community infections like malaria
options.D: To punish workers who have past medical conditions

explanation: A pre-placement check gives us a clear picture of a worker's health before they start a new job, so we can track and protect their health later on.

question: Which of these is a typical part of harsh traditional widowhood practices?

options.A: Forced isolation and denial of basic hygiene and nutrition
options.B: Mandatory medical checkups at a local government clinic
options.C: Immediate financial compensation provided by the extended family
options.D: Celebration of the woman's new status as head of the household

explanation: Sad to say, many widows face difficult isolation, poor sanitation, and restricted food as part of old mourning customs. As nurses, we are here to support them heal!

question: Why is finding out an HIV status early through HCT so helpful for a patient?

options.A: It allows treatment to start before severe immune decline happens
options.B: It prevents any future exposure to opportunistic infections
options.C: It completely eliminates the virus from the bloodstream within days
options.D: It removes all legal restrictions related to employment

explanation: Spot on! Catching the virus early means antiretroviral drugs can protect the immune system before major damage occurs.

question: Why must you check when a patient had their last tetanus shot before stitching up a wound?

options.A: To determine if the patient needs protection against tetanus spores in dirty wounds
options.B: To check how fast the patient's blood will normally clot
options.C: To decide what type of local anesthetic to inject
options.D: To calculate the exact day the sutures should be removed

explanation: Cuts can easily trap dirt and tetanus bacteria. Checking their history helps us know if they need a booster shot to stay safe. Simple and lifesaving!

question: Why can beating too fast (severe tachycardia) actually make the heart less efficient?

options.A: It blocks electrical signals from reaching the ventricles
options.B: It causes the heart muscle to immediately stop receiving oxygen
options.C: It permanently damages the vagus nerve
options.D: It leaves too little time for the heart chambers to fill with blood

explanation: Imagine trying to fill a bucket with water while someone keeps shaking and emptying it too quickly! If the heart beats too fast, it doesn't get enough time to fill up before pumping again.

question: What is the main job of progesterone during pregnancy?

options.A: Relaxing the uterine muscle to prevent premature contractions
options.B: Lowering maternal blood pressure to protect the kidneys
options.C: Stimulating milk production in the maternal breasts
options.D: Triggering the onset of active labor at term

explanation: Progesterone keeps the uterus calm and relaxed (like a peaceful home) so the baby stays safe inside until it is fully ready for birth. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T5#GNS121_U6_T5_h6)

question: Why does the body slow down its metabolism during long periods of starvation?

options.A: To conserve remaining energy stores and prolong survival
options.B: To build up extra muscle tissue in the limbs
options.C: To prepare the digestive tract for a heavy meal
options.D: To increase physical activity levels automatically

explanation: It is a brilliant survival mechanism. When food is scarce, the body dials down its energy use so it doesn't burn through its fat and muscle too fast.

question: What hormonal change helps the digestive tract get back to normal after childbirth?

options.A: A rapid drop in progesterone levels
options.B: A continuous high output of estrogen
options.C: A gradual increase in resting cortisol
options.D: A sudden surge in human placental lactogen

explanation: Once the placenta is delivered, progesterone levels drop fast, allowing the digestive tract to bounce right back to its normal tone.

question: Why are mums who had a very long, exhausting labour at high risk of heavy bleeding after birth (PPH)?

options.A: Her exhausted uterine muscle fails to contract firmly to seal off bleeding blood vessels.
options.B: The placenta always remains completely attached inside the uterus forever.
options.C: Her body stops producing all platelets during the second stage of labour.
options.D: Her blood pressure naturally drops to zero immediately after delivery.

explanation: Correct! Think of the uterus like a muscle that just ran a marathon—by the end, it's too tired to clamp down tightly and shut off the bleeding vessels (uterine atony).

question: Why do animal hookworm larvae cause wandering red lines on human skin instead of a deeper infection?

options.A: Because humans are accidental dead-end hosts where the larvae cannot complete their life cycle
options.B: Because topical soaps paralyze the nervous system of the parasites immediately
options.C: Because human white blood cells instantly freeze the larvae in place under the skin
options.D: Because the larvae lack the physical strength to bite through muscle fascia

explanation: Since humans aren't their normal hosts, the larvae get confused and wander aimlessly in the top layers of the skin. Makes sense when you picture it!

question: Which factor most often decreases the effectiveness of short-acting hormonal methods like oral contraceptive pills?

options.A: Inconsistent daily use or missed doses by the client
options.B: The time of day the client eats her meals
options.C: The client's natural blood pressure levels
options.D: Using the pills during the winter months

explanation: Short-acting methods depend heavily on the user remembering to take or apply them on a strict schedule every day. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h5)

question: Why does blood suddenly rush into a newborn's lungs right after their very first breath?

options.A: The heart rate increases rapidly
options.B: Umbilical cord clamping increases volume
options.C: Pulmonary vascular resistance drops
options.D: Systemic blood pressure decreases

explanation: When the baby takes that first breath and air fills the lungs, the blood vessels inside open right up, letting blood rush in easily to pick up oxygen.

question: A nurse wants to test a new pain reassessment workflow. Which of these is the best way to start a small-scale test?

options.A: Implement the workflow across all regional hospitals starting next Monday

options.C: Test the workflow with three patients on the morning shift with one assigned nurse
options.D: Ask every nurse in the country to write an essay on pain reassessment

explanation: Spot on! Testing with just a few patients and a single nurse lets you see how the workflow feels in real life without creating chaos.

question: What is the most common way people first catch Lassa fever?

options.A: Being bitten by infected mosquitoes at dusk
options.B: Swimming in slow-moving rural rivers
options.C: Eating food contaminated by rat urine or faeces
options.D: Inhaling dust from sweeping dry sandy floors

explanation: Ingesting food or water touched by infected rodent waste is the number one way the virus enters the human body.

question: Which blood tests are most commonly used to evaluate kidney filtration function?

options.A: Serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen
options.B: White blood cell count and hemoglobin
options.C: Serum electrolytes and platelet count
options.D: Prothrombin time and international normalized ratio

question: What is the main cause of painful breast engorgement in the first few days after giving birth?

options.A: Bacterial infection spreading through the lactiferous ducts
options.B: Blockage of the nipple pores by dried colostrum
options.C: A sudden drop in maternal oxytocin during feedings
options.D: Vascular congestion and the initial rush of milk coming in

question: What is the term for white blood cells squeezing through tiny blood vessel walls into injured tissue?

options.A: Vasoconstriction

options.C: Apoptosis
options.D: Diapedesis

explanation: Great job! Diapedesis is just the clever way white blood cells slip out of the bloodstream to join the fight at the tissue level.

question: What is the medical term for completely removing the breathing tube after a patient passes a breathing trial?

options.A: Intubation
options.B: Tracheostomy
options.C: Bronchoscopy
options.D: Extubation

explanation: Extubation simply means taking the breathing tube out once the patient's lungs are strong enough to take over. What a wonderful milestone for recovery!

question: Which symptom is most characteristic of thyroid hormone hypersecretion?

options.A: Rapid weight loss and heat intolerance
options.B: Yellowing of the skin and dark urine
options.C: Low blood pressure and extreme fatigue
options.D: Severe weight gain and cold intolerance

question: Which two measurements do you need to calculate a patient's Body Mass Index (BMI)?

options.A: Weight and height

options.D: Blood pressure and weight

question: Which of these is a classic sign of mastitis in a breastfeeding mother?

options.A: Foul-smelling brownish lochia
options.B: Localized breast redness, pain, and fever
options.C: Complete absence of milk production
options.D: Painless bilateral breast enlargement

explanation: Mastitis means the breast tissue is inflamed or infected. You'll usually spot a painful, red, warm area on the breast along with fever and body aches.

question: What ethical principle ensures that a patient has the right to make their own healthcare decisions without pressure?

options.A: Paternalism
options.B: Autonomy
options.C: Maleficence
options.D: Negligence

explanation: Autonomy refers to the patient's right to self-determination and independent decision-making regarding their treatment and body. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h8)

question: Which of the following is NOT an effective strategy for preventing the spread of gastroenteritis in a community?

options.A: Giving rotavirus vaccines to young infants
options.B: Using over-the-counter antidiarrheal drugs daily
options.C: Washing hands regularly with soap and clean water
options.D: Ensuring access to safe and treated drinking water

question: Why is it so important for a nurse to create a private, gentle setting during a perineal check?

options.A: Bright lighting interferes with visualizing superficial blood vessels
options.B: Perineal tissue is too fragile to touch without numbing agents
options.C: Patients frequently feel embarrassed about intimate examinations
options.D: Hospital policy strictly forbids family members from staying

explanation: Checking someone's private areas can feel very vulnerable. As a caring nurse, building trust and keeping things private helps your patient feel safe and respected.

question: Who should ideally test out a draft questionnaire in the pre-testing phase?

options.A: Only senior professors who have published many research papers

options.D: People who share similar characteristics with your target study group

question: What baseline assessment is most critical to perform and record before starting a gastric lavage?

options.A: Abdominal skin turgor and color tone

options.C: Vital signs and neurological status
options.D: Detailed psychological background history

question: A kitchen worker has a small healing cut on their finger. What should they do before handling food?

options.A: Cover it with a waterproof bandage and wear a clean glove

options.C: Stay home for the entire week until the cut is fully closed

question: What is a very common side effect of post-surgical pain medications that ruins a patient's appetite?

options.A: High fever
options.B: Rapid hair growth
options.C: Increased muscle mass
options.D: Constipation

question: What is the main role of a community health nurse when dealing with child abuse?

options.A: Providing long-term foster care housing

options.D: Population-level surveillance and early intervention

question: Which delivery method is most frequently associated with physical trauma to the foetal skull?

options.A: Spontaneous vertex delivery
options.B: Water birth delivery
options.C: Instrument-assisted delivery
options.D: Elective caesarean section

question: A patient tells you she feels a heavy dragging sensation in her pelvis after having three children. What structures are likely stretched or weakened?

options.A: The Bartholin glands located near the vaginal opening

options.C: The fimbriae at the ends of the fallopian tubes

question: Which piece of equipment attaches to the oxygen source to control gas flow into the tent?

options.A: Pulse oximeter

options.D: Suction canister

explanation: The flowmeter is your best friend for regulating the exact liters per minute of oxygen going into the tent system.

question: A patient calls 4 hours after taking misoprostol saying they have strong cramps, heavy bleeding with small clots, and mild nausea. What do you tell them?

options.A: Tell them to take a double dose of pills
options.B: Send them straight to the ER for a blood transfusion
options.C: Schedule emergency surgery for a hemorrhage

explanation: Cramping and bleeding mean the drug is doing its job! Reassuring the patient builds trust and reduces panic.

question: What is meant by 'brain drain' in the context of Nigerian healthcare staffing?

options.A: The mental fatigue caused by working night shifts
options.B: The gradual decline of memory in elderly patients
options.C: The migration of trained nurses to seek jobs abroad
options.D: The loss of patient records due to poor computer systems

question: What is a major worry when pancreatic fluid leaks from the surgical site after a Whipple procedure?

options.A: Pancreatic fistula and infection
options.B: Immediate high blood pressure
options.C: Chronic kidney stone formation
options.D: Sudden permanent liver failure

question: What is a helpful technique when a Parkinson's patient suddenly 'freezes' and cannot move their feet while walking?

options.A: Firmly push the patient forward from behind to restart momentum
options.B: Instruct the patient to lean backward to shift their center of gravity
options.C: Tell the patient to close their eyes and try to run quickly

question: During a home visit, a nurse sees a strange burn and asks the child, 'How did you hurt your hand?' Why phrase it this way?

options.B: Testing the child's memory for accidental household burns

question: Who is the main age group focused on in the IMNCI strategy?

options.A: Infants in their first year of life

options.C: Toddlers between one and three years
options.D: Children under five years of age

question: What is the main job of cold chain logistics in the food supply chain?

options.A: To keep transport vehicles cool for drivers on long trips
options.B: To freeze-dry grains for underground storage
options.C: To prevent the rapid spoilage of perishable items like milk and meat
options.D: To kill weed seeds in harvested crops before milling

explanation: Cold chain systems use refrigeration to keep perishable foods fresh and safe all the way from the farm to your plate.

question: Which channel is most appropriate when trying to reach healthcare policymakers?

options.A: Public street flyers and local music concerts
options.B: Concise policy briefs and executive reports
options.C: Detailed laboratory notebooks with raw data
options.D: Personal diary entries kept in a desk drawer

question: When reading a measuring tape, why is it important to look straight across at eye level instead of viewing it from an angle?

question: What is the main goal of workplace safety and health in nursing?

options.A: Protecting workers from work-related injuries and illnesses

question: A client with a new physical disability refuses their medications and seems very hopeless. What does this most likely point to?

options.B: A simple misunderstanding of the medication dosage schedule

question: Which of these medications is classified as a long-acting corticosteroid?

question: How do specialized support cohorts differ from standard general groups?

options.C: They meet exclusively inside high-security hospital surgical wards.

question: Why is a structured handover so important when transferring an emergency patient to intensive care?

question: In a female body, which organs make up the 'gonads' part of the HPG axis?

options.B: The fallopian tubes

question: How does the Hib part of the pentavalent vaccine help protect young children?

question: Why are strict aseptic techniques essential when a midwife conducts a delivery in a setting without running water?

options.A: To prevent dangerous infections like neonatal tetanus and puerperal sepsis
options.B: To ensure the baby is born with a lighter birth weight
options.C: To eliminate the need for any postpartum medication use
options.D: To speed up the second stage of normal labor contractions

question: Which of these is a GOOD practice that actually protects a DRF, rather than harming it?

question: Where does Community-Based Rehabilitation mainly take place?

question: What is a windshield survey in community nursing?
