options.C: Feeding the infant warm breast milk
options.D: Minimal external stimuli like touch or noise

explanation: Spot on! Because the calming nerve signals are blocked, even a light touch, a sudden sound, or bright light can trigger violent, painful spasms.

question: What is the main goal of doing a root cause analysis after an incident like a patient fall?

options.A: To permanently close the home health care agency
options.B: To modify nursing protocols and prevent future similar incidents
options.C: The primary purpose is to find a staff member to blame and fire
options.D: To increase the cost of care for future clients

explanation: Root cause analysis isn't about pointing fingers; it's about fixing broken processes so the same accident never happens again. Safety first!

question: Which symptom is a classic sign of an allergic reaction after administering eye drops?

options.A: A slight bitter taste in the back of the mouth
options.B: Mild coolness on the surface of the skin
options.C: Sudden swelling and itching around the eye
options.D: Temporary blurriness right after the drop falls

explanation: Swelling, intense itching, and hives indicate an allergic immune response to the medication ingredients. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T10#GNS122_U1_T10_h8)

question: What is 'elite capture' in the context of community mobilisation?

options.A: When foreign donors pull out all financial support suddenly
options.B: When only wealthy or powerful individuals benefit from or control the project
options.C: When the local police arrest community health workers unjustly
options.D: When traditional healers refuse to speak with modern nurses

explanation: Elite capture happens when powerful community members take over resources meant for everyone. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T1#GNS124_U4_T1_h7)

question: Which type of dietary fiber is especially important to include in the daily meals of older adults?

options.A: Low-residue fiber to completely eliminate bowel movements
options.B: Synthetic fiber powders to speed up stomach emptying
options.C: Animal-derived fiber to build stronger intestinal walls
options.D: High-fiber foods to prevent chronic constipation

explanation: Well done! Because bowel movements tend to slow down with age, fiber is a simple superhero for adding bulk and preventing painful constipation.

question: In nursing, what does the term 'polypharmacy' mean?

options.A: Storing prescription pills in a secure kitchen cabinet
options.B: The use of multiple medications by a single patient
options.C: Taking only one tablet per day for high blood pressure
options.D: Buying drugs exclusively from a wholesale pharmacy

explanation: Polypharmacy simply means taking many drugs at once. It's super common in older adults, but it raises the risk of side effects and drug clashes.

question: An older adult has had a nagging cough and hoarseness for three months that won't go away. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Instruct the patient to purchase over-the-counter cough syrup
options.B: Advise the patient to return only if they cough up blood
options.C: Report these findings to the clinician for further diagnostic evaluation
options.D: Reassure the patient that common colds often last for several months

explanation: Great clinical thinking! A cough that lasts that long without healing is a classic warning sign that needs a proper doctor's assessment right away.

question: What does the term steatorrhea mean during a patient assessment?

options.A: Watery diarrhea resulting from a lack of intestinal mucus
options.B: Painful ulcers forming in the lower part of the esophagus
options.C: Fatty, pale, and foul-smelling stools due to poor fat digestion
options.D: Bloody vomit caused by severe irritation of the stomach lining

explanation: Steatorrhea is the medical term for oily, pale stools that happen when fats pass through undigested due to a lack of bile or enzymes.

question: How has occupational health nursing changed from the 19th century to the 21st century?

options.A: From working exclusively in hospital wards to running corporate legal departments
options.B: From addressing traumatic physical injuries in heavy factories to managing chronic strain and mental wellness
options.C: From ignoring chemical exposures entirely to treating only rare tropical diseases
options.D: From focusing exclusively on boardroom management to supervising mining operations

explanation: While physical safety is still key, today's occupational nurses focus a lot on ergonomics, mental health, and preventing everyday work stress.

question: When should you, as the nurse, do your final dosage calculation?

options.A: Only when the pharmacist calls
options.B: Right before giving the drug
options.C: After a bad reaction happens
options.D: During your annual nursing review

explanation: Always double-check your math right before administration. It is your last chance to catch mistakes before the drug enters the patient's body.

question: A young, unmarried woman leaves a clinic without birth control because the nurse scolds her. What is this barrier called?

options.A: Healthcare provider bias
options.B: Supply chain failure
options.C: Geographic isolation
options.D: Commodity stock-out

explanation: When personal judgments or scolding from healthcare staff stop a client from getting care, that is provider bias. As future nurses, we always want to keep our clinics welcoming and judgment-free!

question: What is the general age range for adolescents according to the World Health Organization?

options.A: 18 to 30 years
options.B: 25 to 40 years
options.C: 10 to 19 years
options.D: 5 to 12 years

explanation: The World Health Organization specifically defines the adolescent period as spanning from 10 to 19 years of age. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h1)

question: What is an important nursing duty when giving a wearable device to a patient?

options.A: Writing custom software code to link the device to the hospital
options.B: Calibrating the internal microchips using a sterile surgical kit
options.C: Teaching the patient how to wear, charge, and sync the device
options.D: Replacing the device hardware components whenever the battery dies

explanation: As a nurse, your guidance is key! Patients need to know how to handle, charge, and sync their devices so the data keeps flowing.

question: What is the main job of the aqueous humor in the eye?

options.A: Supplying nutrients and maintaining eye pressure
options.B: Converting light waves into electrical nerve impulses
options.C: Producing the colored pigments found in the iris
options.D: Adjusting the eye focus for very distant objects

explanation: Think of the aqueous humor as a nourishing liquid bath for the front of your eye, keeping it healthy and properly inflated.

question: What is the main goal when a community nurse acts as an advocate for their patients?

options.A: Performing major surgical operations in local clinics
options.B: Financing private hospitals through personal funds
options.C: Enforcing strict legal penalties against sick community members
options.D: Speaking up for vulnerable groups to improve health resources

explanation: You're doing great! Being an advocate means being a voice for people who might not have the power or platform to speak up for their own health needs.

question: Why can a sudden infection mess up the results of a patient's blood protein test?

options.A: Infections trigger body changes that alter protein levels regardless of diet
options.B: Lab technicians are not allowed to run protein tests during an illness
options.C: Infections destroy all blood drawing needles in the clinic
options.D: Infection automatically cures any existing vitamin deficiency

explanation: Inflammation from an infection can drive blood protein levels down, which might trick you into thinking the patient is starving when they actually have an infection.

question: What is the main difference between meningitis and encephalitis?

options.A: Encephalitis is always caused by fungi, while meningitis is always caused by bacteria.
options.B: Meningitis causes personality changes, while encephalitis only causes stiff joints.
options.C: Meningitis affects the spinal cord exclusively, while encephalitis affects only the skull.
options.D: Encephalitis involves inflammation of the brain tissue itself, while meningitis affects the protective membranes around it.

explanation: Meningitis targets the 'meninges' (the covering layers), while encephalitis targets the actual 'encephalon' (the brain tissue itself). Simple and easy to remember!

question: How do Good Samaritan laws protect you as a nurse during an emergency outside the hospital?

options.A: By shielding them from liability when they give voluntary emergency help
options.B: By granting them the authority to prescribe medications on the street
options.C: By exempting them from following hospital nursing protocols
options.D: By paying all their legal bills if they make a mistake at work

explanation: These laws encourage you to stop and help in an emergency without panicking about being sued for trying your best to save a life.

question: What is a major benefit of doing handovers right at the patient's bedside?

options.A: It prevents doctors from ever entering the patient's room
options.B: It completely removes the need for any written nursing notes
options.C: It reduces the total number of required vital sign checks
options.D: It allows patients to hear their care plan and ask questions

explanation: Bedside handovers make patients part of their own healing journey and help catch any mistakes early!

question: What is the most common cause of new-onset epilepsy in older adults?

options.A: Stroke and cerebrovascular disease
options.B: Congenital metabolic disorders
options.C: Bacterial meningitis
options.D: Idiopathic childhood syndromes

explanation: In older adults, blood vessel issues and strokes are the leading cause of late-onset epilepsy because they can leave small scars in the brain tissue.

question: Which placental hormone creates mild insulin resistance in the mother to guarantee a steady glucose supply for the baby?

options.A: Prolactin
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Human placental lactogen
options.D: Human chorionic gonadotropin

explanation: Human placental lactogen (hPL) cleverly saves more glucose in the mother's bloodstream so it's readily available to cross over and nourish the fetus. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T5#GNS121_U6_T5_h6)

question: How does pulmonary circulation differ from systemic circulation?

options.A: Pulmonary circulation bypasses the right side of the heart
options.B: Pulmonary circulation operates under much lower pressure
options.C: Systemic circulation only carries deoxygenated blood
options.D: Systemic circulation has a shorter pathway than pulmonary

explanation: The pulmonary circuit is a low-pressure pathway because the lungs are close to the heart and offer less resistance than the entire systemic body. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h1)

question: Which substance is most widely available and socially accepted among young people?

options.A: Methamphetamine
options.B: Alcohol
options.C: Heroin
options.D: Cocain

explanation: Correct! Alcohol is the most commonly consumed and socially tolerated substance among adolescents, both globally and right here at home.

question: What is the primary goal of palliative care for an older adult near the end of life?

options.A: Relief of pain and enhancement of comfort
options.B: Immediate restoration of full physical function
options.C: Prevention of normal age-related eye changes
options.D: Aggressive cure of underlying terminal illnesses

explanation: When a disease can no longer be cured, palliative care steps in to make sure the patient is as comfortable, pain-free, and peaceful as possible.

question: Which of these is NOT a risk factor for spreading an epidemic in a community?

options.A: High vaccination coverage
options.B: Poor solid waste management
options.C: Overcrowded living conditions
options.D: Inadequate clean water supply

explanation: Spot on! High vaccination coverage actually protects a community and stops disease spread, making it the correct exception here.

question: Which sign might tell you a patient has developed a collapsed lung (pneumothorax) after a liver biopsy?

options.A: Inability to control their bladder
options.B: Sudden trouble breathing and reduced breath sounds on the right side
options.C: Yellow skin and eyes appearing within an hour
options.D: Painful bruising right on the skin puncture site

explanation: You nailed it! Since the liver sits right under the lung, a misplaced needle can let air into the chest cavity, leading to breathing trouble on that side.

question: What is another common medical name for cervical erosion?

options.A: Cervical carcinoma
options.B: Cervical ectropion
options.C: Cervical dysplasia
options.D: Cervical stenosis

explanation: You will often hear cervical erosion called cervical ectropion in the clinic. It just means the inner cells of the cervix have moved outward a bit. You've got this!

question: What is the main cause of HIV-associated brain and nerve changes?

options.A: Permanent physical brain trauma from falls
options.B: Direct toxicity from antiretroviral pills
options.C: Direct viral invasion and inflammation in the brain
options.D: Chronic lack of dietary vitamin B12

explanation: The virus can cross into the brain early on, causing ongoing inflammation and irritation to nerve tissues.

question: Which of these is a FALSE statement about how HIV spreads that nurses should correct in the community?

options.A: HIV can pass from a mother to her child during breastfeeding
options.B: HIV is easily spread through sharing eating utensils and drinking glasses
options.C: HIV is spread through direct contact with infected blood
options.D: HIV is transmitted through unprotected sexual intercourse with an infected partner

explanation: Correct! Sharing spoons or cups does not spread HIV because the virus dies quickly outside the body and isn't passed through casual saliva.

question: What happens inside the body during disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC)?

options.A: Widespread clotting exhausts platelets and factors, causing severe bleeding.
options.B: The body rapidly produces too many red blood cells.
options.C: Vitamin K is completely destroyed in the stomach.
options.D: Platelets permanently lose their ability to stick together.

explanation: DIC is a wild rollercoaster: the body forms tiny clots everywhere all at once, using up all its platelets and clotting factors. Once they are gone, the patient unfortunately starts bleeding heavily elsewhere.

question: What is the main job of the sticky electrode pads on an AED?

options.A: To monitor the patient's blood pressure and oxygen levels
options.B: To warm up the patient's skin before the shock is given
options.C: To sense the heart rhythm and deliver the electrical shock
options.D: To manually pump blood through the chest cavity

explanation: Think of the pads as the bridge between the patient and the machine: they read what the heart is doing and carry the shock safely into the body.

question: What is a pathological fracture?

options.A: A break caused by a disease that has weakened the bone structure
options.B: A fracture that occurs strictly from a high-speed vehicle crash
options.C: A bone injury that happens exclusively during heavy contact sports
options.D: A hairline crack that cannot be seen on a standard X-ray image

explanation: Think of conditions like osteoporosis or tumors. They weaken bones so much that even normal, everyday movements can cause a break without any major accident happening.

question: Why do nurses check oxygen levels (pulse oximetry) on both a newborn's right hand and their feet?

options.A: To confirm that the umbilical cord was clamped in the correct location
options.B: To compare pre-ductal and post-ductal oxygen levels for abnormal shunting
options.C: To measure how fast blood is traveling through the ductus venosus
options.D: To ensure the liver is receiving enough blood through the hepatic portal system

explanation: Brilliant nursing logic! The right hand gets blood before the ductus arteriosus shortcut, while the feet get blood after it. Comparing them helps nurses catch hidden heart issues early.

question: Why is recording an accurate pregnancy history so important for an expectant mother?

options.A: It guarantees that she will not experience any surgical complications.
options.B: It proves whether her previous babies were born with birth defects.
options.C: It identifies if her past pregnancies put her at a higher medical risk now.
options.D: It determines the exact date of conception for the current pregnancy.

explanation: Knowing the exact number of past viable births helps the healthcare team prepare for potential issues tied to many previous pregnancies, such as bleeding or placental problems.

question: Why does a pregnant woman's body make a lot more blood?

options.A: To lower her core body temperature
options.B: To make up for heavy monthly bleeding
options.C: To prevent swollen veins in her legs
options.D: To supply the growing placenta and baby

explanation: A pregnant body increases its blood volume to make sure the placenta and the growing baby get all the oxygen and nutrients they need.

question: What does a high waist circumference mostly tell you about a patient's health risk?

options.A: Severe protein deficiency and muscle wasting
options.B: A normal and healthy distribution of total body water
options.C: Excess visceral fat linked to heart disease and diabetes
options.D: Chronic lung disease and poor oxygen exchange

explanation: Fat stored around the belly and internal organs is strongly linked to a higher risk of heart problems and diabetes. Excellent clinical insight!

question: What is a core feature of critical thinking in nursing?

options.A: Questioning assumptions and weighing clinical evidence
options.B: Relying solely on what was memorized in school
options.C: Avoiding complex patient care assignments
options.D: Accepting every doctor's order without question

explanation: Critical thinking requires looking deeper into a situation rather than just accepting surface-level appearances. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T7#GNS112_U3_T7_h3)

question: Why does the body keep the testes in the scrotum, slightly cooler than the rest of the body?

options.A: To support healthy sperm production
options.B: To maintain normal urinary flow
options.C: To avoid localized skin irritation
options.D: To prevent excessive testosterone breakdown

explanation: Sperm cells are very sensitive! They need a slightly cooler temperature than standard body heat to grow and develop properly.

question: A nursing mother visits the clinic 6 months after delivery. Why is birth spacing important for her next pregnancy?

options.A: It prevents the infant from developing childhood illnesses
options.B: It allows her body and nutrient stores to fully recover
options.C: It guarantees that the next child will have no health issues
options.D: It eliminates the need for antenatal care later

explanation: Exactly! Giving the body a break restores vital nutrients like iron so the mother is strong and ready for the next pregnancy.

question: Why do deep tissues near the bone often get damaged before the outer skin shows a break?

options.A: Deep muscle and fat layers need oxygen more and are weaker against lack of blood flow than surface skin.
options.B: Bacterial growth starts deep inside the bone marrow.
options.C: Outer skin has a natural defense system that completely blocks pressure.
options.D: Sweat and moisture accumulate underneath the skin layers first.

explanation: Think of deep tissues like hungry muscles near the bone—they need lots of oxygen and give out much faster when blood supply is blocked, even before the outer skin looks broken! [learn more](GNS112_U5_T6#GNS112_U5_T6_h1)
